assertions.description: new RegExp('\A', 'u') compiles: \A is an Assertion in Unicode mode (an unsupporting engine throws SyntaxError: Invalid escape).
new RegExp('\z', 'v') and new RegExp('\Z', 'v') compile: the escapes are valid in v (UnicodeSets) mode too.
assertions.test: (() => { new RegExp('\\z', 'v'); new RegExp('\\Z', 'v'); return true; })()

assertions.description: \A and \z match only the start/end of the whole input even with the m flag: /\Afoo\z/mu matches 'foo' but not 'foo\nbar'.
assertions.test: (() => { const re = new RegExp('\\Afoo\\z', 'mu'); return re.test('foo') === true && re.test('foo\nbar') === false && re.test('bar\nfoo') === false; })()

assertions.description: \A is not a ClassEscape: new RegExp('[\A]', 'u') throws a SyntaxError (with or without the proposal).
Without the u or v flag \A stays an Annex B identity escape: new RegExp('\A').test('A') is true and it does not act as an anchor.
assertions.test: (() => { const re = new RegExp('\\A'); return re.test('A') === true && re.test('') === false; })()
